title: Surprising economics of load-balanced systems
summary: The article explores the counterintuitive economics of load-balanced systems, using queuing theory and Erlang models to explain why capacity scaling doesn't behave as most engineers expect. Marc Brooker analyzes the non-linear relationship between adding servers and actual throughput gains, revealing surprising insights about cost-effectiveness in distributed systems.
problem_solved: Explains why simple linear scaling assumptions fail in load-balanced systems and helps engineers understand the true cost-to-capacity relationship.
why_valuable: Provides mathematical rigor to a common architectural decision, helping teams avoid over-provisioning and understand the diminishing returns of adding capacity in balanced systems.
